quick: 20 mg/m2 IV q3wk with prednisone 10 mg daily
Can cause fetal harm; not used in females
No adjustment for mild-moderate; caution if severe
Reduce dose; contraindicated if bilirubin >3x ULN
CBC frequently, signs of hypersensitivity, LFTs
summary: Cabazitaxel (JEVTANA) is a taxane microtubule inhibitor given IV every 3 weeks with prednisone for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer previously treated with docetaxel. It carries a BOXED WARNING for neutropenia (including neutropenic deaths) and severe hypersensitivity. Premedication and frequent blood-count monitoring are mandatory.
indications: Metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer (mCRPC) previously treated with a docetaxel-containing regimen, in combination with prednisone

dosage.n: Consider primary G-CSF prophylaxis in all patients at this dose

dosage.r: Bilirubin >1 to <=1.5x ULN or AST >1.5x ULN

dosage.n: Avoid concomitant strong CYP3A inhibitors when possible

admin: Administer as a one-hour IV infusion at room temperature using a 0.22 micron in-line filter
Requires two dilutions; do NOT use PVC infusion containers or polyurethane infusion sets
Premedicate at least 30 minutes before each dose to reduce hypersensitivity risk
Final infusion concentration must be 0.10-0.26 mg/mL; do not exceed 0.26 mg/mL
Discard if crystallization or precipitate appears; do not mix with other drugs
Handle as a hazardous anticancer drug; wash skin/mucosa immediately on contact
moa: Cabazitaxel is a microtubule inhibitor that binds tubulin and promotes its assembly into microtubules while inhibiting disassembly. This stabilizes microtubules, arresting mitotic and interphase cellular functions and leading to cancer cell death.

absolute: History of severe hypersensitivity to cabazitaxel or to drugs formulated with polysorbate 80
relative: Age >=65 years (higher rate of fatal outcomes and toxicity)

preg: Can cause fetal harm and loss of pregnancy; in animal studies cabazitaxel caused embryo-fetal death at doses lower than the human dose. Not established for use in females. Advise males with female partners of reproductive potential to use effective contraception.
lact: No human data on presence in breast milk. Because of potential for serious adverse reactions in a breastfed infant, breastfeeding is not advised during treatment.
renal: No dose adjustment needed for mild-to-moderate renal impairment. Renal failure, including fatal cases, has been reported; use caution and monitor in severe impairment or end-stage renal disease.
hepatic: Cabazitaxel is extensively hepatically metabolized. Reduce dose to 20 mg/m2 (mild) or 15 mg/m2 (moderate) impairment. CONTRAINDICATED if total bilirubin >3x ULN (severe impairment).

major: Strong CYP3A inhibitors (ketoconazole, itraconazole, clarithromycin, ritonavir, voriconazole, etc.) - increase cabazitaxel levels; avoid or reduce dose 25%
Live vaccines - avoid in immunosuppressed patients
moderate: Strong CYP3A inducers (rifampin, phenytoin, carbamazepine) - may reduce cabazitaxel exposure
Other myelosuppressive agents - additive bone marrow suppression
minor: Cabazitaxel is a P-gp substrate; clinical interaction risk low at 25 mg/m2
interactions.food: No specific food interactions (IV drug); avoid grapefruit (CYP3A inhibitor) during therapy.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; potential added hepatotoxicity and nausea.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes neutropenia, anemia, thrombocytopenia on CBC; may elevate LFTs.

emergency: Severe hypersensitivity (generalized rash/erythema, hypotension, bronchospasm) - discontinue infusion immediately
Febrile neutropenia / neutropenic sepsis - medical emergency

monitoring: Frequent complete blood counts to detect neutropenia; do not give if ANC <=1,500/mm3
Signs of hypersensitivity during and after each infusion
Liver function tests and total bilirubin before and during treatment
Renal function and hydration status; watch for diarrhea-related dehydration
Urinary symptoms for cystitis, especially after prior pelvic radiation
counsel: Report fever, chills or signs of infection immediately - life-threatening neutropenia can occur
Tell your team about rash, flushing, difficulty breathing or dizziness during infusion
Report severe or persistent diarrhea, vomiting, or signs of dehydration
Report blood in urine, painful urination, or new breathing problems
Use effective contraception (males with female partners); do not breastfeed
Premedication and growth-factor (G-CSF) support may be needed to prevent complications
pk: Immediate (IV); cytotoxic effect over treatment cycles
End of one-hour infusion (Tmax); Cmax ~226 ng/mL at 25 mg/m2
Dosed every 3 weeks; ~80% eliminated within 2 weeks
Store at 25 C (77 F); excursions 15-30 C; do not refrigerate
pearls: BOXED WARNING: neutropenic deaths reported - obtain frequent blood counts; contraindicated if ANC <=1,500/mm3
BOXED WARNING: severe hypersensitivity (rash, hypotension, bronchospasm) - premedicate and discontinue immediately if it occurs
Primary G-CSF prophylaxis recommended in high-risk patients and in all patients at the 25 mg/m2 dose
Contraindicated with prior severe hypersensitivity to polysorbate 80-formulated drugs
Elderly patients (>=65 yr) have higher rates of fatal outcomes and toxicity - monitor closely
Use only PVC-free containers and a 0.22 micron in-line filter
missed: Cabazitaxel is administered in a supervised oncology setting on a fixed every-3-week schedule. Missed or delayed doses are managed by the oncology team based on blood counts and toxicity; patients should not self-administer or reschedule.
overdose: No known antidote; overdose (often from improper preparation) worsens bone marrow suppression and GI toxicity and has caused fatal outcomes. Manage in a specialized unit with close monitoring of vital signs and chemistry; give therapeutic G-CSF as soon as possible and provide symptomatic supportive care.
